title: The VDR rs7975232 Polymorphism Modifies the Association Between Insulin Resistance and Lipid-Related Cardiometabolic Risk Markers in an Ageing Population
content: Background: Ageing is associated with increasing metabolic heterogeneity driven by interactions between adipose tissue dysfunction and altered glucose–lipid metabolism. The vitamin D receptor (VDR) may contribute to individual differences in metabolic regula-tion; however, its role in modifying metabolic responses remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association of the VDR rs7975232 polymorphism with metabolic markers and whether genotype modifies the relationship between glucose–lipid disturbances and metabolic phenotype in older adults. Methods: The study included 95 older adults living in a long-term care facility (mean age 62.5 ± 14.1 years). Anthropometric and fasting biochemical parameters were assessed, and the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), and atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) were calculated. VDR rs7975232 genotyping was performed using real-time PCR. Multivariable linear regression models assessed genotype × TyG interactions after adjustment for age, sex, and waist-to-hip ratio. Results: The rs7975232 genotype was not independently associated with TyG, NEFA, AIP, or other metabolic characteristics. However, significant genotype × TyG interactions were observed for NEFA and AIP in AA genotype carriers compared with the AC reference genotype. A similar interaction was observed for fasting insulin, whereas no significant interactions were found for glucose and only a borderline interaction was observed for log-transformed HOMA-IR. Conclusions: The VDR rs7975232 polymorphism may modify metabolic responses rather than independently determine metabolic phenotype, potentially influencing susceptibility to adverse metabolic alterations in older adults with greater glucose–lipid disturbances.
